headlands.why: the margin continuation, reworked 2026-09-27 (WATER_SHAPE.md section 14, still open after the first design): copying each edge column straight outward at one slope (0.45) read as combed parallel streaks in the close-ups, not headlands. Now the edge is read blurred along itself more the farther out (blur_per_block: a narrow ridge tapers to a point, a broad shoulder holds), at a position that wanders by up to warp_blocks (the outline is not ruled), each stretch of coast reaches out its own distance within reach_range, holding its height and rounding over to the sea at the tip (tip_power), then falling at underwater_fall (long headlands and short ones, bays between), and land carries a little relief. Everything settles in over settle_blocks, so the first margin column is the edge column (M4). The longest reach (185) plus the underwater fall puts every column under y59 inside 200 blocks (M6)

relief.reads_in: tools/worldpainter/export_world.js: the ocean-margin import builds a blank image the size of the canvas (heightmap + 2 x export_margin_blocks) and imports it with onlyRaise, creating only the tiles the landmass lacks; given --margin-image it imports this image there instead, through the same TransformingHeightMap offset and the same importer (the heightmap's own image-to-world line). tools/reexport.py passes it when data/world.json export.margin_relief pins it (path beside the canonical heightmap, sha256)
relief.why: question 1, option A: the seamounts become shape in the same export, and the image also answers the margin join: the revised copy's edge (the new shelves where they reach the border) is carried outward, fading to the y10 floor over 320 blocks. FINDING: land touches the heightmap's edge (north 1,527 columns up to y96, west 444, east 452); today's blank margin drops it to the y10 plain in one column, a cliff of up to 86 blocks at the edge of the map inside the border; the image carries it down to the sea at 0.45 a block. The floor cannot go below y10.09 (image value 0 on the import line), so the_outer_deep's planned y8 plain is y10

B: build them as a block pass after the export (about 3 million blocks each)
